01.r: Solomon calls up a body of workers from the whole people.
01.n: The verb is the ordinary one for 'go up'; in this causative form it means 'make go up', so to raise or levy. The Hebrew puts the verb first: 'and raised the king Solomon'. The JPS numbers this verse 5:27.

03.r: David's son and successor, the king who levies the labour.
03.n: Gesenius: the name means 'peaceable'; he was celebrated for his riches, splendour and wisdom.

04.r: A body of workers drafted for the king's building, not a payment in money.
04.n: BDB: a body of forced labourers, task-workers, a labour-band, formed by levy upon the people, and it names Solomon's levy. Gesenius gives 'tribute', and YLT's 'tribute' and Geneva's 'a summe' follow that sense; but here the levy is counted in men, which suggests labour is meant. The register keeps this word as 'forced labour' to hold it apart from the money words.

07.r: Introduces the size of the levy.

08.r: The same body of workers, now counted.
08.n: The same word as earlier in the verse, now with 'the'.

10.n: The brief's lexicon also gives 'a company of men under one leader' as a sense of this word; here it is the plain numeral.

11.r: The workers counted one by one.
11.n: Singular in Hebrew, 'man', as is usual after a number.

01.n: ἀνήνεγκεν is from ἀναφέρω, to bring up; the brief leaves its dictionary form blank.

02.n: The Greek has only 'the king'; Solomon's name is not in Swete's text here.

04.n: φόρος, tribute: the Greek translators read the word as a payment, the sense Gesenius gives. It is the word our register renders 'tribute' in the New Testament.

_extra.5: καὶ (and): added by the Greek translators; nothing in the Hebrew answers to it.

05.n: ἐκ is 'out of'; the brief's matched dictionary form for it (ἐκπορεύομαι) is loose.

11.n: The brief's text reads αὐτδρῶν, very likely a misprint for ἀνδρῶν, 'of men'.
